newsitem.title: UK: British judge orders anorexic to receive treatment.
newsitem.headline: British judge orders anorexic to receive treatment.

text.p: A British judge ordered an anorexic teenager to be detained in a clinic for treatment, by force if necessary, in a ruling which could have important implications for the rights of the individual.

Judge Nicholas Wall of the High Court Family division said in a ruling published on Wednesday that it was in the young woman's best interest to receive treatment to increase her weight and prevent her from starving herself to death.
"I have no doubt that I have the power not only to direct that she reside in the clinic but also to authorise the use of reasonable force (if necessary) to detain her in the clinic," he said.
Although the ruling was made in a private hearing, Wall gave permission for it to be published because of the important principles involved in the case.

The 16-year-old, who cannot be identified, has suffered from eating disorders since she was 14 and has fought against attempts to be treated. She has run away from clinics and threatened to commit suicide, and has also been sexually abused by her brother.

Wall, who said doctors were convinced she could kill herself in days by refusing to eat or drink, hoped that by forcing her to get treatment she would eventually be discharged from the clinic when she gained sufficient weight.
Doctors at the clinic said they would not treat her without a court order.
The human rights group Liberty criticised the ruling and offered its services to appeal against the decision.
"Unless there is clear evidence that this young woman is mentally ill, the court should not order her detention or treatment," Liberty's director John Wadham said.
"This court order violates her human rights, particularly articles three and five (on inhuman treatment and detention) of the European Convention," he added.
